samples.summary: New agent-facing error codes (`INVALID_FORMAT`, `NOT_LOGGED_IN`) are not added to §10 Error Matrix, the canonical table agents/skills read for codes
samples.evidence: The change introduces two new structured error codes: `InvalidFormatError.code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:15) and `NotLoggedInError.code = 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:36). §8.1 prose mentions them (docs/design/cli.md:722,725) but the canonical enumeration in §10 "Error Matrix" (lines 960-976, which lists INVALID_RANGE, FILE_EXISTS, INVALID_DOCX, etc. with exit codes) was left untouched. An agent reading the matrix to learn the code vocabulary will not find either code, nor the exit code (`ctx list` → 1) they imply.

samples.summary: §8.1 now promises `INVALID_FORMAT` for any unsupported `--format`, but the content/export commands it explicitly names still emit code `ERROR`
samples.evidence: The added prose reads: "An unsupported `--format` value is rejected with `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` rather than ignored. Validation is per-command because `docs`/`slides`/`notes` `content` and `export` deliberately reuse the same global `--format` flag …". That sentence tells an agent those commands also report INVALID_FORMAT, but `parseContentFormat` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:27) throws a plain `Error`, so `outputError`'s `errorCode()` falls back to `'ERROR'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75). The same holds for `detectExportFormat` in packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39 and the slides/notes equivalents. Either those validators should carry `code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` or the doc should scope the claim to `output()` commands only.

samples.summary: Design doc still lists `yaml` as a formatter dispatch target, which strict validation now makes actively wrong
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:647 reads "formatter.ts       Format dispatcher (json | table | csv | yaml)". Before this change an unsupported `--format yaml` fell through and printed `undefined`; now `OUTPUT_FORMATS = ['json','table','csv']` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:7) makes `--format yaml` a hard INVALID_FORMAT error. Since the PR is the one that pins the format vocabulary, this stale line should have gone with it.

samples.summary: The not-logged-in message is duplicated instead of reusing the constant this PR introduced
samples.evidence: status.ts:31 exports `NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE = 'Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.'`, yet `NotLoggedInError` in ctx.ts:39 hardcodes the identical literal, and ctx switch (ctx.ts:95) hardcodes it a third time. The change created the shared constant in the same PR and then did not reuse it, so the three copies can drift.

samples.summary: The two human-facing renderers now disagree on how a single object is laid out
samples.evidence: `formatTable` renders a non-array object transposed as a key/value table (`formatRecord`), while `formatCsv` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:5-10) wraps the same object as one header row + one data row. `status --format table` and `status --format csv` therefore present the same payload in structurally different orientations; a documented convention (or a shared shaping helper) would fit the repo's reuse expectation better.

samples.summary: In-repo comment still asserts the defect this PR fixes ('status ignores --format json and prints prose', 'ground-truth defect #9')
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15-20 documents a deliberate workaround built on the now-fixed behavior. The workaround itself (reading config/session directly) still works, but the justification is stale and will mislead the next reader; the same text is mirrored in .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15.

samples.summary: `ctx list` exit-code change (0 → 1 when logged out) is scope beyond the stated ask
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:80-83 itself flags this as "a behavior change beyond the literal ask". It is defensible (matches `ctx switch`) and disclosed, and the sibling `status` deliberately stays exit 0, but it is an observable contract change for any existing script that ran `ctx list` unauthenticated — worth calling out explicitly in the PR description/release notes rather than only in a task file.

packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:25-32 has the identical shape and error-message template (`Invalid --format "x". Use one of: …`). A tiny shared `parseEnum(value, allowed, ErrorCtor)` would remove the copy and let both vocabularies carry INVALID_FORMAT consistently.

finding.summary: New agent-facing error codes (`INVALID_FORMAT`, `NOT_LOGGED_IN`) are not added to §10 Error Matrix, the canonical table agents/skills read for codes
finding.evidence: The change introduces two new structured error codes: `InvalidFormatError.code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:15) and `NotLoggedInError.code = 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:36). §8.1 prose mentions them (docs/design/cli.md:722,725) but the canonical enumeration in §10 "Error Matrix" (lines 960-976, which lists INVALID_RANGE, FILE_EXISTS, INVALID_DOCX, etc. with exit codes) was left untouched. An agent reading the matrix to learn the code vocabulary will not find either code, nor the exit code (`ctx list` → 1) they imply.

verdict.reason: The literal observation is accurate — §10's table (docs/design/cli.md:960-976) has no INVALID_FORMAT/NOT_LOGGED_IN row — but the harm it asserts is already guarded in the same canonical doc, and the finding's premise about §10 being the canonical code enumeration is false. (1) Counterexample: docs/design/cli.md:721-722 documents `ctx list` emitting `"code": "NOT_LOGGED_IN"` AND "exits `1`", and cli.md:724-728 documents `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` with the per-command-validation rationale — so both the code vocabulary and the exit code the reviewer says an agent "will not find" are present in docs/design/cli.md §8.1. (2) §10 is a scenario table (columns Case|Exit|Code|Message), not an exhaustive code registry: pre-existing codes SESSION_EXPIRED (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:132), HTTP_ERROR/INVALID_RESPONSE (packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:164,201), INVALID_PPTX (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-import.ts:61) and NOT_FOUND (packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:28, used in §8.1's own example at cli.md:699) all lack matrix rows. A repo-wide grep for "Error Matrix" returns exactly one hit — its own heading — so nothing designates it canonical. (3) Agent-facing surfaces do not consume it: packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md has no code list, and packages/cli/README.md:109-115 is explicitly illustrative ("e.g., INVALID_DOCX, TYPE_MISMATCH, CONFIRMATION_REQ") with an "ERROR" fallback. (4) Design-doc discipline is satisfied: the canonical subsystem doc was updated in place (no parallel doc), matching the task's acceptance item at docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:96 ("docs/design/cli.md prose references updated"); no acceptance criterion requires a §10 row. What remains is a doc-completeness preference (add two rows to a non-exhaustive table), which is minor/nit under this lens and never blocks.

finding.summary: §8.1 now promises `INVALID_FORMAT` for any unsupported `--format`, but the content/export commands it explicitly names still emit code `ERROR`
finding.evidence: The added prose reads: "An unsupported `--format` value is rejected with `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` rather than ignored. Validation is per-command because `docs`/`slides`/`notes` `content` and `export` deliberately reuse the same global `--format` flag …". That sentence tells an agent those commands also report INVALID_FORMAT, but `parseContentFormat` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:27) throws a plain `Error`, so `outputError`'s `errorCode()` falls back to `'ERROR'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75). The same holds for `detectExportFormat` in packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39 and the slides/notes equivalents. Either those validators should carry `code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` or the doc should scope the claim to `output()` commands only.

verdict.reason: The quoted prose exists verbatim at docs/design/cli.md:724-728 and states unconditionally that an unsupported --format is rejected with code INVALID_FORMAT, while the very next clause names docs/slides/notes content and export. Only InvalidFormatError (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:14-22), thrown by parseOutputFormat/format (36-56), carries that code. The named commands' validators throw plain Errors — parseContentFormat (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:25-32), detectExportFormat (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39-54), packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:26, packages/cli/src/notes/content.ts:10, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:202, packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:195 — and errorCode() (formatter.ts:70-76) falls back to 'ERROR' for them. No wrapper at the call sites attaches a code. The code is present as described, is reachable, and design-doc accuracy/spec conformance is in this lens's lane (the task checklist item "docs/design/cli.md prose references updated" is precisely what is inaccurate). No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Design doc still advertises the removed `*` active marker in the command tree
finding.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:267 `│     ├── list                             List workspaces (* = active)`. The change deletes `formatWorkspaceList` and its `*` prefix (ctx.ts) and updates the examples at cli.md:455 and the §8.1 prose, but the canonical command tree at line 267 still documents the old prose output. The task doc's checklist item "`docs/design/cli.md` prose references updated" (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:96) is therefore only partly satisfied, leaving the design doc self-contradictory about the contract this PR changes.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence is not in the repository. docs/design/cli.md:267 does NOT read "List workspaces (* = active)"; it reads "List workspaces (`active: true` marks the current one)" — already updated to the new contract. A grep for `= active` / `* = active` across docs/ returns zero hits in docs/design/ (only unrelated activeIndex/activeTabId code snippets in archived task files), so no residual `*` marker survives anywhere in the design docs. All active-related lines in cli.md are mutually consistent: :267 documents the `active: true` flag, :455 shows `# [{ id, name, active }]`, and §8.1 (:710-722) describes the output() routing — the doc is not self-contradictory. This matches the code: packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:11-32 defines `WorkspaceRow { id, name, active: boolean }` via buildWorkspaceList, whose docstring at :19-21 explicitly says the active workspace "is flagged by the `active` field rather than a `*` prefix". `formatWorkspaceList` appears nowhere in source — its only hit repo-wide is a historical mention of its deletion in the task doc (20260806-...todo.md:36). The checklist item "docs/design/cli.md prose references updated" (todo.md:96) is fully satisfied, and todo.md:103-104 shows the author additionally swept the published sibling page for this exact `*`-marker issue. With the alleged stale string absent, there is no design-doc-discipline or spec-conformance gap.
